page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton ARM64 processors. The instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this architecture ensures dedicated CPU allocation without resource sharing or hyperthreading overhead.

The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. This local storage provides low-latency, high-speed read and write operations directly attached to the host. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

The primary tradeoff of the c9gd.large is its low memory-to-CPU ratio, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. However, the combination of dedicated ARM64 cores and local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that require fast temporary storage. Suitable workloads include distributed build systems, containerized microservices, video encoding, and localized caching databases.
